column1:
Cautiously constructive, tempered by tighter bank credit from the July 2024 SLOOS. The FOMC held the target range at 5.25–5.50% and highlighted “further progress” toward 2% and a “better balance” of risks, but will wait for “greater confidence” that disinflation is durable before cutting. Implementation remains in the post-2008 framework (IOER 5.4%, ON RRP 5.3%, standing repo 5.5% minimum) with balance-sheet runoff continuing ($25B Treasuries, $35B agency MBS caps).

What the July 2024 SLOOS adds:
- C&I: Banks, on net, continued to tighten standards and report weaker loan demand across firm sizes, citing economic outlook and risk tolerance. Loan rate spreads remain elevated.
- CRE: Standards tightened further and demand softened, with particular caution around office; consistent with ongoing CMBS/CRE stress.
- RRE: Generally tighter or unchanged-to-tight standards and softer demand for most mortgage categories.
- Consumer (credit cards, auto, other): Further tightening and weaker demand; special-question indicators point to stricter underwriting (e.g., higher spreads, tougher score and payment criteria).

Implications: SLOOS indicates credit supply remains a drag even as macro data show solid activity and easing inflation. That mix supports the Committee’s patient, data-dependent stance: tighter bank lending and soft loan demand are disinflationary but add downside growth risk, arguing against near-term cuts until confidence in 2% is firmer.

Bottom line: Maintain a mildly positive read on growth/disinflation, but downgrade the tilt modestly to reflect persistent bank tightening and weak loan demand signaled by SLOOS.
